Sign Up All AI in Tech AI in Politics Nvidia Scandal 4 Posts Sort by Newest Oldest incoming update… 1 hour ago Pinned FAA’s $875M AI system faces scrutiny after nationwide ground stop, but officials deny connection 
 The Federal Aviation Administration’s new $875 million artificial intelligence system is facing renewed scrutiny following a nationwide flight ground stop that disrupted air travel Friday, although federal officials say the technology was not responsible.
 The FAA’s SMART system , designed to predict air traffic congestion and help controllers manage flight routes, was rolled out nationwide Nov. 10, just three days before the widespread disruption.
 Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and other federal officials have said the ground stop was caused by communications problems involving an aging telecommunications network and maintenance work, not the AI system.
 Still, the rollout has raised questions about AI’s role in aviation safety. House Democrats requested a federal audit of SMART last month, citing concerns about reliability, limited controller training and the potential for AI-generated errors.
 The system, developed by Air Space Intelligence, analyzes roughly 200 data streams, including weather, flight paths and controller staffing, to recommend adjustments. Human air traffic controllers retain final decision-making authority, according to the FAA.
 The Associated Press contributed to this report. 
 Posted by Stephen Sorace Share 28 mins ago Dem senator accuses Lutnick of ignoring warnings over Nvidia chip exports to China 
 Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., is accusing Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to act on national security warnings about advanced Nvidia chips reaching China , arguing that his department’s inaction has jeopardized America’s technological edge in artificial intelligence.
 In a Nov. 15 letter to Lutnick, the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee alleged that the Commerce Department ignored repeated warnings from federal agencies about Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company at the center of the Nvidia controversy.
 “Despite these warnings, the Department of Commerce delayed action on repeated national security warnings, putting America’s technological advantage in AI at risk,” Cantwell wrote.
 Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., speaks during a press conference following the weekly policy luncheon, on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., on June 3, 2025. (Reuters/Annabelle Gordon) Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday on CNBC that four federal agencies had supported placing Megaspeed on a trade blacklist for months, but Commerce had not acted.
 Cantwell also accused Commerce of suspending an investigation into Megaspeed and raised concerns about potential financial conflicts involving the Trump administration’s 25% fee on certain Nvidia chip exports to China.
 Fox News Digital reached out to the Commerce Department for comment.
 Megaspeed has not been found to have violated U.S. export restrictions and said Thursday that it takes its obligations under American export control laws "extremely seriously" and remains committed to working "constructively and transparently" with the U.S. government.
 The Associated Press contributed to this report. 
 Posted by Stephen Sorace Share 1 hour ago Megaspeed says Alice Huang, linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, left company in 2025 
 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang embraces Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang after delivering his keynote speech at COMPUTEX 2024 in Taipei, Taiwan, June 2, 2024. (Reuters/Ann Wang) Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International says Alice Huang , a Chinese businesswoman whose reported relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sparked U.S. national security concerns, left the company last year as it launches an internal investigation into allegations surrounding its operations.
 Alice Huang departed Megaspeed on Aug. 30, 2025, and no longer holds a role at the company, Megaspeed told The Associated Press on Sunday.
 The company, which has faced scrutiny over allegations that it circumvented U.S. export restrictions to supply advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese firms, said it retained outside legal counsel to conduct an internal investigation.
 Megaspeed denied wrongdoing, maintaining that it operates a legitimate business and that media reports about its operations contain claims unsupported by verifiable evidence.
 The announcement comes days after Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO following reports of an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials have suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence.
 The Justice Department has not determined whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy, and Beijing has rejected the allegations as unsubstantiated.
 Posted by Stephen Sorace Share 1 hour ago Trump administration to name Nvidia, other AI giants as ‘national champions’: report 
 A logo of Nvidia is displayed at at the Computex Taipei exhibition, one of the world's largest computer and technology expos, in Taipei, Taiwan, Wednesday, June 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Chiang Ying-ying, File) The Trump administration is preparing to designate Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic among more than two dozen artificial intelligence “national champions” as part of a push to help American tech companies expand overseas and compete with Chinese rivals, according to a new report.
 The initiative would give selected companies access to expedited export license approvals, federal financing and government support for international business, The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the plans.
 Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to announce the designations within the next week, although the timing could change, according to the report.
 The program, first unveiled last year, aims to make it easier for foreign governments and businesses to purchase American AI technology, including advanced chips, AI models and other products, as Washington seeks to strengthen U.S. leadership in the global AI race.
 The expected announcement comes amid heightened scrutiny of Nvidia following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang and renewed national security concerns surrounding the company’s advanced chip exports to China.
